title: OpenAI Responses interop profiling and remediation pathway
creator: Aisha Carter
description:
Goal: Produce a concrete, prioritized remediation pathway that maps crucial OpenAI Responses behaviors to Redwood’s Responses API semantics, quantifies fidelity gaps, and prescribes runtime and SDK mitigations to preserve customer contracts during upgrade or adapter deployment.

Scope:
- Inventory behavioral differences for streaming framing, event ordering, partial content, final summary events, and error semantics.
- Map tool/function-calling contract differences (function schema, invocation lifecycle, tool errors, and async tool flows).
- Capture structured output / JSONL differences, acceptance heuristics, and canonicalization rules.
- Produce a graded compatibility matrix (behavioral delta, customer impact, mitigations).

Out of scope: internal model implementation changes, upstream OpenAI negotiation, or long-running re-architectures beyond a 6-week remediation window.

Deliverables:
1) Compatibility matrix CSV/Confluence page listing event names, example payloads, and recommended shim transformations.
2) A small adapter library (runtime-level patch + SDK helpers) with feature flags to enable/disable specific translations.
3) Test harness with golden transcripts and fuzzed stream events for canary testing.
4) Rollout plan with metric guards and automated rollback triggers.
tasks: Run a corpus collection job to capture 500 representative OpenAI Responses transcripts across streaming, function calls, and structured outputs.
Produce an event-by-event diff tool that highlights dropped tokens, re-ordered events, and schema mismatches.
Design adapter transformations for: streaming 'delta' chunks, function call open/close events, tool error propagation, and structured JSON object normalization.
Implement canary flags in runtime that enable adapter for 1% traffic; instrument latency and error deltas.
Add contract tests to SDK that assert round-trip fidelity for function-calling and structured outputs.
Prepare Confluence spec, example PRs, and README for platform and SDK teams.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix covers 100% of collected corpus event types and includes example payload transformations.
Adapter reduces customer-visible behavioral deltas to low or none for P0/P1 patterns validated by golden transcripts.
Canary rollout instruments guardrails: token-loss rate, malformed-json rate, average latency delta; all are reported to console dashboard.
SDK contract tests pass in CI and new adapter is feature-flagged with rollback knob.
Runbook updated with developer troubleshooting steps and decision tree for escalation.
risks: Adapter introduces additional CPU work during streaming which could increase tail latency under high concurrency.
Edge cases in function-calling async flows (tool initiated callbacks) may not be reliably representable without protocol extensions.
Aggressive normalization of structured outputs may silently change user payload semantics for downstream tooling.
Inadequate test corpus may miss rare but customer-visible event sequences leading to regression after rollout.
test_plan: Generate golden transcripts from corpus and assert byte-for-byte equivalence after adapter for controlled inputs.
Fuzz stream reordering and chunk-splitting scenarios to validate adapter resilience to partial events.
Simulate tool failures and network interruptions to verify retries, error propagation, and idempotency semantics.
Add canary traffic with mirrored recording to compare OpenAI-origin run side-by-side with Redwood adapter run for the same prompts.
Add a synthetic workload in staging that measures tail P95/P99 latency and token-processing CPU across adapter ON/OFF.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal QA with adapter enabled for platform engineers (0% customer traffic).
Phase 1: Canary (1% traffic) with metrics alarms for token-loss > 0.1%, malformed-json > 0.05%, latency delta > 15ms.
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 10% with daily review and false-positive check against golden transcripts.
Phase 3: Tiered rollout by customer segment (non-enterprise -> enterprise) with documented opt-out and compatibility report.
Rollback criteria and playbook published in runbook with contact list.
